item1.justification: The trace correctly applies Graham/KSR factors (scope and content, differences, PHOSITA level, secondary considerations) for all §103 rejections and uses a claim-specification support analysis for §112 rejections, invoking the proper legal framework throughout.

item2.justification: Each rejection specifically cites claim language (e.g., 'semi-local data sector,' 'predetermined tolerance,' 'projected speed/rate/size') alongside named prior art references (US-2014121932-A1, US-2012281091-A1, US-2014278090-A1) and identifies the specific disclosures relied upon for each element.

item3.justification: Claims found to have only partial anticipation at §102 (e.g., claims 2, 3, 5, 9) are then rejected under §103 or §112 at the office action stage with additional rationale explaining what the prior art teaches and why combination or a written description problem applies, maintaining consistency without contradiction.

item4.justification: With strictness=0.875 (high), the examiner rejects all 19 pending claims (2–20) with no allowances, resolves every ambiguity toward rejection, and even converts novel claims (5, 9, 11, 15, 16) into §112 rejections rather than allowing them, fully consistent with a veteran strict profile.

item5.justification: The final decision to reject all claims follows directly from the accumulated stage analyses: §103 findings with confidence mostly ≥0.80 and §112 rejections for claims lacking specification support, with the summary explicitly tying the decision to the strictness calibration and stage-level conclusions.
